oneliner.t: Former Navajo Nation president (2019–2023) and vice president (2015–2019) from Tuba City who lost AZ-02 to Eli Crane 54.5%–45.5% in 2024. Now the 2026 Democratic nominee and a DCCC 'Red to Blue' candidate, he faces Crane again in a rematch, along with Libertarian Curtis Goodwin.

born.note: Birthplace in both; exact date from Wikipedia only.

profile.residence_note: Home address not documented. His consulting LLC is located in Flagstaff/Coconino County per his disclosure.

upbringing.t: Born in Tuba City and raised in Shonto on the Navajo Nation; he is Áshįįhí (Salt People), born for Ta'neeszahnii (Tangle clan). His campaign says he grew up on dirt floors without electricity or running water and overcame addiction as a young man; these are his own accounts. He attended Northland Pioneer College and earned a B.S. in political science and a Master of Public Administration at Northern Arizona University. He was Shonto chapter vice president and a Navajo County supervisor before joining the Navajo Nation Council in 2007.

profile.office_years_note: Navajo Nation Council 2007–2015, vice president 2015–2019, president 2019–2023. Navajo County supervisor and Shonto chapter vice president years are not documented and not counted.

platform.t: Water: protect Arizona's Colorado River share; faults Crane's handling of Colorado River cuts.
Cost of living: says rural Arizonans pay too much for child care, housing, groceries and health care; frames the race around a class divide and criticizes 'elites.'
Voting: calls Arizona 'ground zero' for attacks on election security; notes that voting is already hard on tribal lands.
Immigration: calls the system broken and backs comprehensive reform.
Crane: says the incumbent has not brought enough federal money to the district and is 'too extreme' for most Arizonans.
Same-sex marriage: endorsed legalizing it on the Navajo Nation during his 2022 campaign.

promises.t: Oppose partisan attacks on mail-in voting and Arizona's election infrastructure.
Pass comprehensive immigration reform with 21st-century security technology, more border agents and caseworkers, and a path to citizenship.
Secure 'real resources' to fight the opioid epidemic in rural and tribal Arizona.
Make sure infrastructure dollars reach old roads, flood control and new community centers, and win Arizona its 'fair share.'
Work with the Bureau of Land Management on wildfire protection.
Work with both parties to lower costs and invest in water systems, roads and bridges.

checks.legal: News search: an Oct 2018 Navajo Times report says a citizen (Frances Lester) filed a complaint with the Navajo Nation Ethics and Rules Office. It alleged that then-Vice President Nez used his purchase card for a family Disney World trip and used over $600,000 in tribal travel funds for his presidential campaign. The matter was at intake; no outcome was found, and Nez's response was paywalled. It is an allegation, not a finding, and is not entered in legal[]. No other cases found. CourtListener/Justia and Navajo Nation courts were not searched directly.
checks.foreign: 2026 candidate report read directly: no foreign assets or income. Consulting clients include the Hopi Tribe and Navajo-affiliated entities, which are domestic tribal nations, not foreign governments. FARA not searched.

research_notes: Rematch of 2024. Polls: a Nez internal poll (Aug 2026, 500 likely voters) had Crane 46%, Nez 44%; Arizona Agenda says other polls show Crane ahead, one by 11. Republicans hold an 11-point registration edge. Ruben Gallego campaigned with him in Prescott. If elected he would be the first Native American to represent Arizona in Congress. In 2022 he and his family were nearly struck when an SUV drove through a Gallup parade (he was not at fault; excluded from legal). az-races.json says he was unopposed in the 2026 primary; Ballotpedia's stale page listed Eric Descheenie as a primary candidate. His spouse Phefelia Nez's Kennedy Center trustee appointment (2022) is her record, not his.
